interface.name: kora_halo_header_manager_v1

description.summary: opt into the Halo's drag strip over the client

interface.description:
The compositor floats the Halo above every server-side decorated window, clear of the client content and outside the window's geometry; window placement keeps room for it. By default nothing of the Halo reaches into the client. A Halo-aware client may opt into overlay mode, which also gives the Halo a drag strip across the top of the client, and keeps its own controls clear of that strip.
This does not negotiate server-side decorations: clients must still use xdg-decoration for that. Client-side decorated windows, fullscreen edge reveal, and embedded surfaces are unaffected. If the global is absent, clients must work with ordinary server-side decoration geometry.

entry.name: reserved
entry.summary: Halo above the client, no strip over it (default)

entry.name: overlay
entry.summary: Halo above the client plus a drag strip over its top edge

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroying this object does not change any surface's mode.

request.name: set_mode

description.summary: choose layout before the initial surface commit

request.description:
The surface must have an xdg_toplevel role. Call after get_toplevel and before the initial wl_surface.commit, so the first configure accounts for the requested header placement. A request after the initial configure is a protocol error. The mode persists for the lifetime of the wl_surface, including unmap/remap cycles. No other surface, including a transient child, inherits this mode.
In overlay mode the client is responsible for keeping its controls clear of the drag strip. Neither mode hides the compositor's Halo or changes where it is drawn.
